description: The US Environmental Protection Agency's emergency response programme for drinking water and wastewater utilities publishes six short case studies, each as a PDF dated 14 July 2022 with a video, on how utilities handled supply chain problems. They cover Des Moines Water Works and a possible carbon dioxide shortage, the Poarch Creek Indians Utility Authority and short supplies of chlorine and soda ash, Klamath Falls building a water department warehouse to hold inventory, the Northeast and Merrimack Valley chemical consortium in which Massachusetts and New Hampshire utilities bulk buy chemicals and laboratory supplies, the Trinity River Authority's actions after Winter Storm Uri, and Fort Bragg's operational changes to offset geographic isolation. Coverage: six US utilities, with a short lessons-learned narrative each. Access: free PDFs and videos; the licence is not stated on the page read. Caveats: the PDFs themselves were not opened, so figures inside them are not reproduced here. It supports chemical supply disruption and utility inventory policy studies, and relates to the TCEQ Winter Storm Uri review and the post-hurricane supply chain case study in the catalogue.
